title: MV Downloading a website hosted game?

posts.author: ModderOfGames
posts.body:
I ask this primarily for the sake of preservation, as a preface.
in 2016, the people behind Ao Oni released an updated version done in RPG Maker MV, only ever in Japanese and only ever hosted on a website
That website... no longer exists, and the only way you can play it is via an Internet Archive link. And even when you could, it was quite buggy and would fail to load assets all over the place.
I want to download it in full so I can open it up in MV, patch up the holes, and (hopefully) eventually make it more accessible for people to play ten years on
unfortunately, as I said, it was only ever hosted as a website, and I cannot for the life of me figure out how I'd go about downloading it... aside from playing through the whole game and downloading each asset one-by-one, as there's no way to force Chrome to cache every single asset at once (afaik anyways), and even then it wouldn't really matter, as some things simply do not work at all, meaning at best it'd end up being incomplete
So I come here asking: is there any way to download an entire game that is only hosted as a website?
Here's the Internet Archive Link
if you wish to either play it yourself, or want to see if there is any way to download it
Any help would be soso much appreciated, thank you!!
~ Mars

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
Speaking theoretically, it should, in fact, be totally possible. After all, every asset used in the game is referenced
somewhere
in the data and script files, and the data files have fixed filenames. The script files
don't
have fixed filenames, but they're all referenced from one place, so you can easily gather a list of the filenames. So, in theory, if you download just the data files, you can compile a complete list of every other asset, and then you can download those one by one. It's far from easy (there are tons of different ways in which the assets can be referenced), but it should be possible in theory.
However, I have a strong suspicion that this isn't going to work very well for you. You see, the way the Internet Archive works is that it follows links and uses that to determine what to cache. But those assets are not linked from anywhere in the game's main page. There's a high chance that some of the assets are missing from the Internet Archive… as it seems you've already noticed. Unless the missing assets are pure RTP, I'd say they're very likely lost forever, unless one of the original developers has them and is willing to share.

posts.author: JorgeMaker
posts.body:
I really appreciate initiatives to preserve games, especially when it comes to RPG Maker, so your post caught my attention and I decided to check out the game.
I extracted all available files using the
Wayback Machine’s CDX Server API
and performed a basic reconstruction so that the project can be opened correctly in RPG Maker MV.
I tested only the first minute of the game, which seems to work fine. However, I noticed that at least some maps were not archived, and this could potentially extend to other data.
You can download the extracted project
here
. Good luck!

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body: Ah, yes – maps are another thing that could easily be missed. You can trivially construct a list of all maps that exist if you have the MapInfos.json (which is loaded by default even though nothing in the engine uses it, so you probably do), but there are no direct HTML references to them, so they might not have been archived.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
Yes, maps that are completely unused would probably be lost; but it's not limited to that. Honestly, probably any map could be lost. None of the maps are referenced by the HTML, after all. In theory, it might even be possible to lose the starting map.
I don't know exactly how the Internet Archive works though. The fact that it has any of this data suggests that it does more than just follow links, and that might be enough to at least guarantee the starting map exists, if nothing else.

posts.author: ModderOfGames
posts.body:
from what I've found while digging, both before and after the archive, anything that is strictly *required* to be loaded, gets loaded (though given some delay, especially with the archive)
I can view all cached files with inspect element, and even download images and audio files, but I'm limited to what has been loaded while I've had the site open, I can't find a way to force my browser to cache the whole thing at once, which makes sense
and something I've noticed with both versions too, occasionally it will "fail to find files", but only because it took too long to load them, rather than them not existing. it happens with plugins on launch sometimes and that's all I've ever noticed it, but I'd assume this is another thing that extends to more files
EDIT:
Been messing around with the files that Jorge posted and playing through it to see what is all there, and so far all I've noticed that is missing from the main game has been certain audio files, thankfully being ones either present in base RPG Maker XP, or are just from the original version of Ao Oni.
I haven't actually tinkered in the database too much quite yet, but I have noticed a staggering number of empty maps, but am still unsure of... at what point the maps start being completely blank
EDIT 2:
Alright, final edit for now I think, but it seems that (at the very least when it comes to maps), the CDX Server API downloaded the first ~56 or so that got loaded? as those are the only ones that are in the folder
there's missing audio and graphics all over the place as well, some of which I've started to take note as being from original content new to this version, which is... unfortunate, to say the least
